items.title: [OPINION] GTA 6’s Ultra-Realistic Life-Sim Elements Could Possibly Limit the Series’ Classic Fun
points: The GTA series has fundamentally always been about stealing cars, robbing stores, escaping the cops, and killing people with minimal consequences.
You rob another car, the cops catch you, and you do it all over again without a care in the world.
But this obsession with making GTA 6 feel hyperrealistic and immersive could end up taking away what makes the series so much fun in the first place, and here’s why.
I had similar issues in Red Dead Redemption 2’s life-sim elements, but they were negligible since it’s a Red Dead title.
There’s a lot more to these life-sim and roleplay elements in GTA 6.
It feels more like an evolution of the horse’s stamina mechanic from Red Dead Redemption 2 than a genuinely meaningful addition.
Next up in the coterie of life-sim roleplay elements is how GTA 6’s cash acts like the real thing.

items.title: BJP, JD(S) leaders cannot tolerate guarantee schemes reaching all beneficiaries: Karnataka CM Shivakumar

items.title: A devotee dies while climbing up Deviramma Betta in Chikkamagaluru
points: A devotee collapsed and died while climbing Deviramma Betta to visit the hilltop temple at Mallenahalli near Chikkamagaluru on Sunday (November 8, 2026) morning.
The deceased has been identified as Lakshman, 35, of Kanyadi in Dakshina Kannada district.
He was climbing the hill from the Mallenahalli side when he collapsed.
Fire and Emergency Services personnel, who were stationed along the trail to assist devotees, carried the body down the hill.
It was later shifted to the district government hospital in Chikkamagaluru.
Lakshman, who worked for a private company in Bengaluru, came to visit a relative in Huvinahalli.
The Deviramma temple atop the hill is open to the public only during the annual festival, which began on Saturday (November 7).
The Chikkamagaluru district administration and the police have made security arrangements and put safety measures in place for the smooth conduct of the festival.

items.title: One child dead, 269 treated for burn injuries in T.N. during Deepavali
points: File | Photo Credit: AP One child succumbed to burn injuries, and 269 people were treated for firecracker-related burns across Tamil Nadu during the Deepavali festivities, according to official data tracking emergencies over a 24-hour window.
As per the official bulletin, the state 108 emergency ambulance network received 16,079 calls between 7 a.m. on November 7 and 7 a.m. on November 8.
Of the total distress calls, 2,475 were related to accidents, 396 for minor injuries, and 98 specifically for burn injuries.
The admissions included 956 for accidents, 321 for minor injuries or assaults, and 110 for burn injuries.
Demographic data for burn injuries shows that men formed the largest group of victims, with 92 treated as outpatients and 76 admitted as inpatients.
The Thanjavur Government Medical College Hospital recorded the highest patient volume for burns, accidents, and minor injuries, treating 36 outpatients and admitting 87 inpatients.

items.title: A rare red Diwali: Sensex ends Muhurat trading lower for only the eighth time in 30 years
points: MUMBAI: The 8 November Diwali Muhurat trading session marked a muted start to Samvat 2083, with the benchmark Sensex closing 0.04% lower.
Over the past 30 years, the Sensex has ended the Muhurat trading session in the red just eight times, including Sunday's decline.
The Sensex fell 28.62 points, or 0.04%, to close at 80,999.40 on Sunday.
The Nifty 50 has lost 1.1% since the previous Samvat year, reflecting a subdued year for equities.
On Friday, the last trading session of Samvat 2082, the Sensex advanced 2.2% to 81,028, while the Nifty rose 2% to close at 25,030.35.
Trades placed during Sunday's Muhurat session will be reflected in investors' accounts on the next trading day, Monday (9 November), which coincides with the first day of the new year.

Participation in this year's Muhurat trading session was higher than last year's, with NSE recording equity cash market turnover of ₹23,374 crore, compared with ₹19,714 crore in the previous year's session, according to exchange data.

items.title: Wanted in over 30 heinous criminal cases, carried ₹5 lakh reward: Punjab gangster Gurwinder alias Afridi brought back to India
points: Gangster Gurwinder alias Afridi, wanted in more than 30 heinous criminal cases, was brought to India from Ethiopia by the Punjab Police on Sunday.
Afridi, a resident of Tut village in Tarn Taran district, carried a ₹5 lakh reward announced by the Punjab government.
Officials said he was taken into custody by the state police at Delhi airport during the intervening night of November 7 and 8 and was being brought to Punjab to face legal proceedings.
He is reportedly wanted in more than 30 serious criminal cases, including five murder cases, attempted murder, extortion and offences under the Arms Act.
In June 2024, Amritsar Rural Police arrested Jaswinder Singh, alias Munshi, describing him as a key accused in the case.

These include the killings of Sarpanch Rajwinder, alias Raj Talwandi, in October 2024; a 12-year-old in March 2025; Vicky Chugh in March 2025; Jaswant Singh in May 2025; and Congress block president Gurmel Singh in September 2025.

items.title: AI analytics, technological upgrades to drive retail investor experience in new Samvat: NSE CEO Ashishkumar Chauhan
points: Highlighting the exchange's digital initiatives, Chauhan announced major technological upgrades aimed at improving the experience of the country's growing retail investor base.

Turning to market conditions, Chauhan expressed confidence in India's fiscal discipline and economic resilience despite volatile crude oil prices and foreign institutional investor (FII) outflows.

However, India is currently managing its fiscal deficit remarkably well," Chauhan said.

On retail trading trends, Chauhan highlighted a shift towards responsible investing, observing that market participants were increasingly adopting defined-risk strategies in derivatives rather than taking unhedged risks.

items.title: Jaipur Cafe Owner Ambushed, Beaten With Iron Rods By Attackers
points: A cafe owner, who was walking home from work, was ambushed by motorcycle-borne attackers in Jaipur and was seriously injured after being beaten with iron rods.
Mayank Gopalia, the owner of Oven The Bakery Cafe, was attacked with deadly force.
A video of the incident, which has gone viral, shows the men first hitting him on the head and then on his back and legs.
The victim lost consciousness after the attempted murder.
Gopalia, seriously injured in the attack, was admitted to Fortis Hospital.
According to the employees of the cafe, an employee, Shabana Khan's husband, Shahrukh, could have attacked Gopalia.
After a dispute at the cafe, they had threatened to kill Mayank.

items.title: Kerala Govt Orders Ethanol Percentage Check in Petrol After Karnataka Finds 31.2 % Ethanol
points: The controversy surrounding ethanol blending in petrol has now reached Kerala, with the state government ordering inspections to check whether oil companies are supplying fuel with ethanol content exceeding the prescribed limits.
The move comes just days after the Karnataka government claimed that laboratory tests had found ethanol levels as high as 31.2% in petrol samples collected from different parts of the state.
According to Food and Civil Supplies Minister Rizwan Arshad, independent laboratory testing found ethanol content above the prescribed 20% level in several samples.
The highest reading was 31.2% in a regular petrol sample from an Indian Oil Corporation outlet.
An HPCL Power sample reportedly recorded 30.5%, while other samples from BPCL, Nayara Energy and Shell also showed ethanol levels above 20%.
Indian Oil, BPCL and HPCL have questioned the sampling and testing methodology used by Karnataka, maintaining that their E20 petrol meets the prescribed quality standards.

Key areas of review included deregulation and business reforms, financial management, development priorities, sectoral councils, administrative reforms and Sixth Schedule Autonomous Councils, he said.

items.title: Bright Outdoor Media moves to BSE, NSE main boards, eyes expansion in digital advertising
points: Bright Outdoor Media Ltd has moved its shares to the main boards of the BSE and the National Stock Exchange.

Bright Outdoor Media Ltd has moved its shares to the main boards of the BSE and the National Stock Exchange, marking a step up from the SME platform where it became India's first listed outdoor advertising company in March 2023.
Founded in 1980, Bright Outdoor Media operates more than 1,350 hoardings across strategic locations and owns over 50 large-format digital LED billboards in Mumbai.

The move to the main boards follows its debut on the BSE SME platform on March 24, 2023, when it became the first company from India's out-of-home (OOH) advertising industry to enter the stock market.
Bright Outdoor Media is also seeking to broaden its offerings through its 'Bright 360' initiative, which aims to combine different advertising formats and branding services under one platform.

The five baby orangutans were rescued from Bichitrapur forest in Balasore district on September 8 and subsequently shifted to Nandankanan Zoo, where they have been kept in quarantine.

points: It appears that foreign portfolio investors (FPIs) have changed their bearish stance towards the Indian stock market, buying domestic equities aggressively last week and pouring in a massive ₹45,970 crore in just five trading sessions.
The shift in sentiment boosted the Nifty 50 by 8.6% during the week, marking its strongest weekly performance since February 2021.
The rally also helped the index pare its year-to-date losses to 4.21%.

items.title: Phantom Blade Zero Review — A Combat Masterpiece
points: The year 2026 has been a breakthrough for action RPGs.
We have already had the likes of Onimusha: Way of the Sword and Control Resonant performing beyond expectations.
However, gamers had been waiting for one action RPG, and it was Phantom Blade Zero.
So, did Phantom Blade Zero meet its promised hype?
After playing almost 40 hours of Phantom Blade Zero, I can most definitely say that it has the best combat I have seen in any recent action RPG releases, but sadly that’s not the entire picture.
In terms of responsiveness for high-speed combat, Phantom Blade Zero is in a class of its own, untouched by any other game.
The combos in Phantom Blade Zero are very similar to fighting games, but a tad bit less complicated.
Weapons in Phantom Blade Zero have gone beyond that, not only having unique abilities, but also having unique animations for each.

items.title: Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei's Representative Wishes Indians A Happy Diwali
points: Dr Abdul Majid Hakim Elahi, the representative in India for Iran's Supreme Leader, Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei, extended his heartfelt Diwali wishes to the people of India.
During a four-day visit to the shrine of 'Shaheed-e-Salis' in Agra, Dr Elahi conveyed his festival greetings and prayed for the continued happiness of all Indians.
He remarked that Diwali is a festival of joy and light, expressing his hope that every Indian remains prosperous and that both India and Iran continue to prosper.
Describing the occasion as a "festival of light," he offered his congratulations and wished everyone a long and healthy life.
Agra is home to the shrine of the renowned 'Shaheed-e-Salis,' who was martyred during the Mughal era.

items.title: Stock markets end marginally lower in special Muhurat trading, snapping 7-day rally
points: Benchmark indices Sensex and Nifty ended marginally lower in the special Diwali Muhurat trading session.
Benchmark indices Sensex and Nifty ended marginally lower in the special Diwali Muhurat trading session on Sunday amid profit-taking by investors after a seven-day rally.
After starting the special trading session to mark the beginning of Hindu calendar Samvat 2083 on a bullish note, the 30-share BSE Sensex failed to sustain the rally.
In the 30 Sensex firms, Mahindra & Mahindra, InterGlobe Aviation, Trent, Infosys, Bharti Airtel and Axis Bank were among the biggest laggards.
Unlike regular trading days, when equity markets operate from 9:15 am to 3:30 pm, Muhurat trading runs for a shorter period.

items.title: Banner seeking info on four wanted terrorists surfaces in Srinagar's Lal Chowk
points: A banner seeking information about the whereabouts of four terrorists wanted by security forces surfaced on Sunday (November 8, 2026) in Srinagar's Lal Chowk area.

A flex banner was found hanging early in the morning on the wall of Pratap Park in Srinagar, seeking information about the four terrorists, including Mohammad Lateef Bhat, involved in the killing of a cop in Anantnag in July this year.
The others include Bilal Ahmad Mir, Mohammad Umar Mir and Abid Qayoom Lone, all from Baramulla district.

While Bhat, a resident of Kulgam district in south Kashmir, is active in the Kashmir Valley, the other three terrorists are currently believed to be operating from Pakistan-occupied Jammu and Kashmir (PoJK), officials said in Srinagar.

"Anyone who can provide credible information regarding the movement/presence of these terrorists, the identity of the informant will be kept strictly confidential and a handsome reward will be given for reliable information," the banner reads.
Comments have to be in English, and in full sentences.

items.title: Supreme Court Questions Delhi’s Pollution Curbs, Says Bumper-To-Bumper Traffic Causing More Pollution
points: The Supreme Court has questioned why Delhi-NCR continues to suffer severe air pollution despite years of vehicle restrictions and other measures.
During a hearing on November 6, Chief Justice Surya Kant pointed to bumper-to-bumper traffic on roads connecting Delhi with Gurugram, Noida, Ghaziabad and other neighbouring cities.
Delhi's Air Quality Index reached 391 on Friday, November 6, close to the severe category that begins at 401.
Of the city's 59 monitoring stations, 30 were reporting severe pollution at 9am.

Under the revised GRAP rules, Stage III restrictions apply to BS3 petrol and BS4 diesel four-wheelers in Delhi and specified NCR districts, including Gurugram, Faridabad, Ghaziabad, Gautam Buddh Nagar and Sonipat.
Separate entry restrictions introduced on November 1 apply to non-BS6 petrol and diesel vehicles registered outside Delhi, with specified exemptions.
The Centre told the court that steps already included geo-tagging pollution-under-control certificates, restricting entry of certain vehicles and acting on reports of visibly polluting vehicles.

items.title: Woman held for joining son, friends in assaulting 17-year-old boy over Instagram messages in Kochi
points: A 40-year-old woman was arrested on Sunday for allegedly joining her son and his friends in assaulting a 17-year-old boy over a dispute linked to Instagram messages in Edappally, police said.
The assault took place on Saturday at the woman's rented house on Changampuzha Road in Edappally North, leaving the boy injured, they said.
According to police, the boy and the woman's son had studied together until Class 10 and were now doing Plus Two in different schools.
The boy and some of his friends had created a common Instagram account for online gaming.
When he recently regained access, he found that his friends had sent obscene messages to several women through the account.
On Saturday, one of the friends called him to a location in Elamakkara to settle the dispute.
Based on his complaint, Elamakkara police registered a case on Sunday and arrested the woman.
The case has been registered under Sections 3(5), 110, 127(2), 189(1)(c), 190, 296(b) and 351(3) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita.

items.title: 25-year-old stabbed to death in Bengal flat, live-in partner, her mother arrested: Cop
points: A 25-year-old resident of Garia in West Bengal’s South 24 Parganas district was stabbed to death inside a rented flat on Saturday night, police said on Sunday.
Police also arrested the victim’s live-in partner and her mother as prime suspects.
“Sarthak Sarkar was stabbed inside his rented flat in the Narendrapur area.
Other residents of the multi-storey building said they heard Sarkar quarrelling with his live-in partner Sanchalika Basu, 24, and later found him lying on his bed with multiple wounds.
According to the police, Sarthak Sarkar’s father and sister, who live in Barasat in North 24 Parganas district, said his phone was unreachable for several hours on Saturday evening.
They said Sanchalika informed Sarthak’s sister over the phone that he had been taken to the hospital in critical condition.
Sanchalika and her mother Moumita Basu were arrested on Sunday based on charges filed by the victim’s family,” the officer added.
“Some scratch marks were found on Sanchalika Basu’s neck, indicating a struggle during the alleged murder,” the officer added.

items.title: Why did RR Kabel share rally 8% during Muhurat Trading despite weak market sentiment — what triggered the surge?
points: Cable and wire manufacturer RR Kabel's shares ended the special one-hour Muhurat Trading session on Sunday, November 8, with a solid 8% jump to settle at ₹2,073, even as the frontline indices closed in the red.
Around 1.4 million shares changed hands across the BSE and NSE during the session, nearly twice the stock's weekly average trading volume, according to Trendlyne data.

The shares had suffered significant losses following the company's September-quarter results, ending October with a 19% decline and extending their losing streak to a second consecutive month after falling 14% in September.
Despite the recent weakness, the stock remains up 42% in 2026, supported by the gains accumulated during the first half of the year.
The company lowered its FY27F volume growth guidance to around 14-15%, from the earlier estimate of 16-18%, citing market volatility and quarterly fluctuations.
For the September quarter, RR Kabel reported a 55.7% year-on-year increase in consolidated net profit to ₹180.6 crore, compared with ₹116 crore in the year-ago period.

items.title: J&K: 4 police personnel, including SHO, injured as bus rams police vehicle in Ramban

The bus hit the police vehicle at a crossing, causing it to overturn on the highway.
Four police personnel, including the SHO Inspector Vicky Thapa were injured in the incident.
They were taken to District Hospital Ramban for treatment, officials said.
Mr. Sharma, who stopped his convoy and joined the rescue efforts after witnessing the accident, said the police vehicle suffered extensive damage, but all personnel on board were safe.
The manner in which the bus hit the police vehicle underscores the need for greater vigilance at crossings, particularly those along national highways,” he told PTI.
Medical Superintendent of District Hospital Ramban, Dr. Mohammad Rafi Wani, said the condition of the four police personnel was stable.

items.title: Emami vs Dabur Q2 results: Which FMCG giant wins on profit, revenue and dividend? Check target, upcoming record dates
points: Emami vs Dabur Q2 results: Shares Emami and Dabur India Limited surged nearly 7% over the last week after both the FMCG giants announced their second quarter results for the financial year 2026-27.
While Emami reported a marginal 1.92% annual decline in its consolidated net profit, Dabur India’s net profit after tax (PAT) surged by 12% on a yearly basis.
Emami’s net profit declined 1.92% on an annual basis to ₹145.50 crore for September quarter of financial year 2026-27.
Dabur India’s profit increased 12.09% to ₹498.57 crore in Q2FY27.

Meanwhile, Dabur India’s board of directors approved ₹3.50 per share dividend for FY27 and fixed November 9 as the record date.
Motilal Oswal gave a ‘Neutral’ rating for Dabur India stock with a target price of ₹425 per share.

items.title: Why Bertie thinks investors should be like drones
points: As an investor, Bertie thinks of himself as a drone.
Not that he harbours any delusions of being able to fly, at least not while sober.
The analogy stems from his self-image as someone who can survey the investment landscape from a few hundred feet before swooping down to examine an area of interest more closely.
Bertie's professional engagements last week reflected the wide canvas he likes to paint on.
A Wall Street bank was hosting an exclusive meeting with a visiting global macro economist for a select group of high-powered chief investment officers (CIOs).

The Wall Street bank, which had itself been bailed out twice, was displaying uncharacteristic financial prudence, Bertie thought, by making him sit through a 56-slide presentation before he could get to his beloved pralines.
Having heard enough global economists over the years, Bertie knew that it was only a matter of time before the discussion turned to India's macroeconomic fault lines.

items.title: Muhurat Trading 2026: Samvat 2082 ends, Samvat 2083 begins - Sensex, Nifty end in red first time after 2017 | Reasons
points: Muhurat Trading: Indian equity markets began Samvat 2083 on a weak note on Sunday, November 8, 2026, as the BSE Sensex and NSE Nifty 50 ended the special Diwali Muhurat Trading session in the red, snapping an eight-year winning streak.
The 30-share Sensex closed 28.62 points lower at 80,999.40, while the Nifty 50 settled 6.65 points down at 25,023.70.
This marked the first Muhurat Trading session to end in negative territory since 2017.
However, broader markets outperformed, with the Nifty Midcap index ending 0.13% higher and the Nifty Smallcap index gaining 1%.
During the previous Samvat year, Samvat 2082, the BSE benchmark Sensex declined 3,398.32 points, or 4%, while the Nifty fell 838.25 points, or 3.24%.
In the previous Muhurat Trading session in 2025, the Sensex had gained 63 points to close at 84,426, while the Nifty 50 advanced 25 points to settle at 25,868.
The rupee opened 2026 at 89.97 against the US dollar before weakening 7.9% to an all-time low of 97.12 on May 20, 2026.

items.title: Punjab anti-drug activist Parvinder Singh Jhota cremated 26 days after being shot dead
points: The mortal remains of slain anti-drug activist Parvinder Singh Jhota, whose murder 26 days ago triggered protests and a political row, were consigned to flames at his native place here on Sunday.
Jhota was shot dead on October 13 in broad daylight at a medical store in a busy marketplace in Mansa town while he was hosting a Facebook Live session.
Jhota's father, Bhim Singh, called upon the youth of Punjab to pledge against drug abuse, saying his son gave up his life fighting against the scourge.
The joint action committee (JAC), also known as the Parminder Singh Jhota Insaaf Action Committee, is a coalition of various social organisations and activists formed in Punjab after Jhota's murder.

Jhota's body was brought to PGIMER Chandigarh from the mortuary of Civil Hospital in Mansa in the early hours of Friday, after his family ended their 22-day agitation and agreed to a post-mortem following a meeting with Punjab government representatives on…

items.title: Three family members, including 20-day-old baby, killed as house roof collapses in Kanpur
points: Three members of a family, including a 20-day-old baby, were killed in Uttar Pradesh' Kanpur when the roof of a room in their house collapsed on Sunday morning.
The deceased have been identified as Vinodini Shukla, 60, her daughter-in-law Anshika 28, and 20-day-old grandson.
Harsh Shukla 32, who was also present inside the room when the roof caved in, sustained minor injuries.
Family members and neighbours rushed to remove the debris and pulled out the occupants who were then taken to Kalyanpur Community Health Centre.
According to a relative Manoj Bajpai, the family were busy with their morning chores on Diwali, while Harsh and his mother were sitting in the room.
Anshika was feeding their newborn and other members of the family, including Harsh's father Avadhesh Shukla, 65, and younger brother Raju, 29, were in another room when the roof collapsed.
The house, owned by Avadhesh, is around 35 years old.
DCP West SM Qasim Abidi said police had received information about three deaths following the roof collapse.

items.title: Telangana celebrates Deepavali with traditional fervour; Guv visits Bhagya Lakshmi temple

Dressed in new clothes, people offered prayers at temples and indoors, decked their homes with lamps and flowers, and burst crackers.
Governor Shiv Pratap Shukla, Chief Minister A.

Governor Shiv Pratap Shukla, accompanied by his wife Janaki Shukla, visited the Bhagya Lakshmi temple at Charminar here, a message issued by Lok Bhavan said.
The Governor wished that the country and Telangana would prosper with the Goddess’s blessings, and that people would be blessed with happiness, peace and good health.
He hoped people would celebrate the festival with joy and enthusiasm, lighting up their homes and surroundings with lamps.

items.title: 10 Hybrid Cars And SUVs Ranked By Mileage: MG Hector Tomahawk PHEV Leads
points: Currently, manufacturers such as Maruti Suzuki, Toyota, Honda, Renault and MG offer a number of hybrid cars and SUVs in the country.
Currently, the hybrid vehicle which offers the highest mileage in India is the MG Hector Tomahawk PHEV.
This SUV comes equipped with a plug-in hybrid powertrain which comprises a 1.5-litre petrol engine paired with an electric motor and a large 20.5 kWh battery pack.
MG claims that the Hector Tomahawk offers a combined fuel efficiency of over 40 kmpl.
Next up is the Renault Duster Strong Hybrid, which offers a claimed fuel efficiency of 29 kmpl.
The third SUV with the best mileage is the Maruti Suzuki Victoris Strong Hybrid, which offers an ARAI-certified mileage of 28.65 kmpl.

Being the rebadged version of the Grand Vitara, the Toyota Urban Cruiser Hyryder also delivers an identical claimed mileage of 27.97 kmpl.

items.title: India-bound Toyota Land Cruiser FJ Likely To Get A Diesel Engine
points: GaadiWaadi - Lack of a diesel engine is one of the main gripes about Toyota’s new global C-segment rugged SUV The India-bound Toyota Land Cruiser FJ ticks nearly all the main boxes for a rugged SUV, but performance is one of its main downsides.
More than the sheer lack of power, purists particularly miss the availability of a diesel engine option.
For the uninitiated, the Toyota Land Cruiser FJ is a body-on-frame C-segment SUV that slots below the Toyota Fortuner.
Most customers prefer diesel engines in such vehicles for their strong pulling power at low engine speeds and higher fuel economy.

In a recent interview with Cars.co. za, Andrew Kirby, the President and CEO of Toyota’s South African subsidiary, said that “there’s a good likelihood” for the introduction of a diesel engine for the Land Cruiser FJ.
However, Kirby indicated that, at least in South Africa, the potential diesel engine is a few years away.

items.title: Tata Teleservices shares jump 6% in Muhurat Trading, extend 4-day rally to 23% | What's driving the surge?
points: Tata Teleservices (Maharashtra) shares surged over 6% during Muhurat Trading on Sunday, 8 November, extending their winning streak to a fourth consecutive session.
The stock has gained more than 23% over these four trading sessions, despite the company disclosing a regulatory penalty imposed by the Department of Telecommunications (DoT).
The telecom operator received a penalty of ₹25,000 from the DoT on 6 November 2026, for alleged violations of certain provisions of its Unified License Agreement.
The company disclosed the development in a stock exchange filing under Regulation 30 of the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015.
The company reported a net loss of ₹59 crore for the July-September quarter of FY27, narrowing significantly from a loss of ₹321 crore in the corresponding quarter last year.
Tata Teleservices share price today opened at ₹39.77 apiece on the BSE, the stock touched an intraday high of ₹42.29 apiece and an intraday low of ₹39.62 per share.

items.title: Armed Maoists eliminated, but ‘dimagi Naxals’ remain a threat: PM Modi
points: Addressing security personnel during Diwali celebrations at a Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF) camp in Karanpur in Chhattisgarh’s Bastar district, Modi said identifying and defeating such elements was essential to securing the country.
He described the elimination of armed Maoists as a victory for the government’s policies and strong political will, but cautioned against complacency.
Armed Naxalites have disappeared from the forests, but ‘dimagi Naxals’ have taken control of several organisations,” he said.
Describing the fight against Maoist violence as a major challenge, he said more than 230 districts across nearly 20 states were once affected by Naxalism.
Modi said the lack of political will to tackle the menace had been addressed in 2014, when people gave him an opportunity to serve the country.
He also said that, for the first time in 47 years, not a single Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF) personnel had been killed in the line of duty during the preceding year.

items.title: Lower crude, global stability to drive market growth in new Samvat: ANMI President Kamlesh Shroff
points: India's macroeconomic environment is poised for robust growth, projected at over seven percent, bolstering equity markets.

Retail and domestic institutional investors are actively engaging despite foreign investor withdrawal.
Clarity from recent US elections is predicted to alleviate geopolitical tensions, boosting business confidence and anticipation of renewed foreign investment in Indian markets.

items.title: Indian economy to grow faster, foreign capital returning to markets: NSE CEO Ashishkumar Chauhan
points: India's economy is projected to experience faster growth due to strong macroeconomic fundamentals and increased foreign interest.
The Managing Director of the National Stock Exchange highlighted that the country is managing fiscal pressures effectively.
Domestic financial savings have significantly increased, reaching nearly USD 1.4 trillion annually.
Furthermore, foreign institutional investors are showing renewed enthusiasm for Indian markets ahead of the new Samvat year.
